name: Kirkland
seo_title: 8 Christmas Events for Kids in Kirkland, WA 2026
seo_desc: 8 Christmas events for kids in Kirkland, WA, 4 free: Photos with Santa at The Village at Totem Lake and more.
lede: Kirkland does Christmas on the waterfront and downtown: a free WinterFest and tree lighting around Peter Kirk Park, city bonfires on the beach when the Christmas Ship sings offshore, and cozy Santa mornings at the community centers.
celebrates: The season opens downtown with WinterFest at Kirkland Urban, where families take photos with Santa in his sleigh and watch ice sculpting before the Kirkland Downtown Association lights the city tree in Peter Kirk Park. Along Lake Washington, the City of Kirkland lights free Community Bonfires at the Park in waterfront parks when the Argosy Christmas Ship stops to sing. Google Holiday Lights brightens Feriton Spur Park every night into January. The city's parks department fills North Kirkland Community Center with a Snowflake Ball and Cereal with Santa, and the Kirkland Community Foundation hosts a Teddy Bear Tea Party with Mrs. Claus.
lastyear: In 2025 Kirkland Urban held WinterFest on Saturday, November 29, from 4 to 8 pm on its plaza at 425 Urban Plaza. The program listed photos with Santa in his magical sleigh, costumed characters, live ice sculpting, snowfall on the promenade, kids' crafts, alpacas from Enchanted Farms and complimentary s'mores from Marsh and Mallow Co. As evening fell, the Kirkland Downtown Association hosted the annual Tree Lighting Celebration steps away in Peter Kirk Park, with festive vendors and live music.
facts: Kirkland is named for Peter Kirk (1840 to 1916), a British steel mill owner from Workington, England. In 1888 Kirk and his partners formed the Moss Bay Iron and Steel Works and planned Kirkland as the Pittsburgh of the West, giving streets British names such as Piccadilly and Oxford. A nationwide financial collapse in 1893 ended the mill before it opened. Kirkland incorporated in 1905, and its ferry landing became the most popular on Lake Washington, reaching Seattle in just over 30 minutes.
trains: Kirkland's best known rail line is now a trail. The Cross Kirkland Corridor is a 5.75 mile stretch of the old Eastside Rail Corridor, first built in 1904 as the Lake Washington Belt Line between Renton and Snohomish to haul coal and lumber. From 1993 to 2007 the Spirit of Washington Dinner Train ran on those tracks, and the city removed the rails in 2013. For a real ride, Link light rail's 2 Line reaches Redmond, and the Northwest Railway Museum in Snoqualmie runs its Santa Train each December.

kidfact: Kirkland was supposed to be a steel town. Peter Kirk wanted to build a giant steel mill and called his new town the Pittsburgh of the West, but the mill never opened.
faq: Where is the Kirkland Christmas tree lighting?

The Kirkland Downtown Association lights the city tree in Peter Kirk Park, at the Peter Kirk Park Plaza on Third Street downtown. It happens on the evening of WinterFest, the free holiday festival on the Kirkland Urban plaza next door, so families can see Santa in his sleigh and then walk over to watch the tree light up.
Can you see the Christmas Ship from Kirkland?

Yes. The Argosy Christmas Ship stops off several Kirkland waterfront parks each December, and its choir sings carols toward shore. On those evenings the City of Kirkland lights free Community Bonfires at the Park, each lasting about 20 minutes. Bonfires can be canceled for weather or a burn ban, and the city keeps a hotline with updates.
Where can kids see Santa in Kirkland?

Santa poses in his sleigh at WinterFest on the Kirkland Urban plaza, joins families at the city's Cereal with Santa pajama breakfast at North Kirkland Community Center, and visits Reindeer and Reels in Peter Kirk Park. The Kirkland Community Foundation's Teddy Bear Tea Party features Mrs. Claus and her elves instead of Santa.
Are there free Christmas lights in Kirkland?

Yes. Google Holiday Lights at Feriton Spur Park on 6th Street South is free and stays lit every evening from early December into early January. The opening night includes carolers, a lighting ceremony, sweet treats, a petting zoo and a photo booth, so it is a good first visit for younger kids.

The magic runs from November 21 (Photos with Santa at The Village at Totem Lake) through January 8, with Photos with Santa at The Village at Totem Lake (from November 21), WinterFest at Kirkland Urban and Tree Lighting at Peter Kirk Park (November 28) and Community Bonfires at the Park for the Christmas Ship (from November 28) along the way. We check every date on the host’s own website or an official city calendar, and each listing links straight there. For the rest of the state, see our Washington Christmas events for kids guide.
